# Regulatory requirements matrix (spec 13, 26.7)

An engineering summary to organise the work, **not legal advice**. Qualified counsel must confirm what applies, the wording and the dates (spec 26.7). The status here is the **starting** status; the live status, owner and evidence are on the **Compliance** page. "Implemented" means the software supports it, not that the hospital is compliant.

## United States

| Code | Law | Citation | Requirement | What the law asks | What HIMS does | Starting status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| HIPAA-SEC-RISK-ANALYSIS | HIPAA Security Rule | 45 CFR 164.308(a)(1)(ii)(A) | Security risk analysis | Assess risks to the confidentiality, integrity and availability of electronic patient data. | Threat model and risk register (Compliance page, docs/compliance/threat-model.md). The hospital must complete it for its own site and hosting. | In progress |
| HIPAA-SEC-RISK-MGMT | HIPAA Security Rule | 45 CFR 164.308(a)(1)(ii)(B) | Risk management | Reduce risks to a reasonable and appropriate level. | Risk register with treatment, owner and review date. | In progress |
| HIPAA-SEC-ACTIVITY-REVIEW | HIPAA Security Rule | 45 CFR 164.308(a)(1)(ii)(D) | Information system activity review | Regularly review audit logs and access reports. | Audit log screen, tamper check, access reviews. The hospital must run the reviews. | In progress |
| HIPAA-SEC-OFFICER | HIPAA Security Rule | 45 CFR 164.308(a)(2) | Security official | Name one person responsible for security. | Compliance officer role in HIMS. The hospital names the person. | Not started |
| HIPAA-SEC-WORKFORCE | HIPAA Security Rule | 45 CFR 164.308(a)(3), (a)(4) | Workforce access management | Give staff only the access they need; end it promptly when they leave. | Roles and scopes, default deny, periodic access reviews, cover with end dates, sessions ended when employment ends. | Implemented, not verified |
| HIPAA-SEC-TRAINING | HIPAA Security Rule | 45 CFR 164.308(a)(5) | Security awareness training | Train all staff, including how to report incidents. | Report-an-incident button for all staff. The training itself is the hospital's. | Not started |
| HIPAA-SEC-INCIDENTS | HIPAA Security Rule | 45 CFR 164.308(a)(6) | Security incident procedures | Identify, respond to, document and mitigate incidents. | Incident log with deadlines and docs/compliance/incident-response-runbook.md. | Implemented, not verified |
| HIPAA-SEC-CONTINGENCY | HIPAA Security Rule | 45 CFR 164.308(a)(7) | Contingency plan | Backups, disaster recovery and emergency-mode operation, tested. | Planned with the hosting stage (backups, restore drills, RTO/RPO). | Not started |
| HIPAA-SEC-BAA | HIPAA Security Rule | 45 CFR 164.308(b), 164.502(e) | Business associate agreements | Sign agreements with vendors that handle patient data. | Vendor list in docs/compliance/vendors.md. The contracts are the hospital's. | Not started |
| HIPAA-SEC-PHYSICAL | HIPAA Security Rule | 45 CFR 164.310 | Physical safeguards | Protect facilities, workstations and devices. | Hosting provider and hospital responsibility; automatic sign-out helps workstations. | Not started |
| HIPAA-SEC-ACCESS-CONTROL | HIPAA Security Rule | 45 CFR 164.312(a) | Technical access control | Unique user IDs, emergency access, automatic logoff and encryption where appropriate. | Unique accounts, 30-minute sign-out, permission checks on the server, encrypted secrets. Still to come: emergency access (Phase 2), encryption at rest (hosting). | In progress |
| HIPAA-SEC-AUDIT-CONTROLS | HIPAA Security Rule | 45 CFR 164.312(b) | Audit controls | Record and examine activity in systems holding patient data. | Append-only audit log with a tamper-evident chain. Chart-read auditing comes with Phase 2. | Implemented, not verified |
| HIPAA-SEC-INTEGRITY | HIPAA Security Rule | 45 CFR 164.312(c) | Integrity | Protect patient data from improper change or destruction. | Versioned edits, nothing deleted, audit tamper check. Clinical amendments come with Phase 2. | In progress |
| HIPAA-SEC-AUTHENTICATION | HIPAA Security Rule | 45 CFR 164.312(d) | Person authentication | Verify that people are who they claim to be. | Strong passwords, two-factor sign-in for privileged roles, sign-in throttling. | Implemented, not verified |
| HIPAA-SEC-TRANSMISSION | HIPAA Security Rule | 45 CFR 164.312(e) | Transmission security | Protect data sent over networks. | Production settings force HTTPS and secure cookies; TLS is set up at hosting. | In progress |
| HIPAA-SEC-DOCUMENTATION | HIPAA Security Rule | 45 CFR 164.316(b) | Policies kept six years | Keep written policies and required records for six years. | docs/compliance holds the drafts; the hospital adopts and keeps them. | In progress |
| HIPAA-BREACH-INDIVIDUALS | HIPAA Breach Notification Rule | 45 CFR 164.404 | Tell affected people | Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 days after discovering the breach. | Incident log sets the 60-day deadline and alerts before it passes. | Implemented, not verified |
| HIPAA-BREACH-HHS | HIPAA Breach Notification Rule | 45 CFR 164.408 | Tell HHS | 500 or more people: within 60 days of discovery. Fewer: within 60 days after the year ends. | Incident log works out the right deadline from the number of people. | Implemented, not verified |
| HIPAA-BREACH-MEDIA | HIPAA Breach Notification Rule | 45 CFR 164.406 | Tell the media | More than 500 residents of a state or area: within 60 days. | Incident log adds this step above 500 people. Counsel checks the per-state count. | Implemented, not verified |
| HIPAA-PRIV-NPP | HIPAA Privacy Rule | 45 CFR 164.520 | Notice of Privacy Practices | Give patients the notice and record acknowledgment. | Recorded at registration in Phase 2 (design decision D9). | Not started |
| HIPAA-PRIV-MIN-NECESSARY | HIPAA Privacy Rule | 45 CFR 164.502(b) | Minimum necessary | Use and show only the patient data needed for the task. | Least-privilege roles and scopes today; patient-level rules designed for Phase 2. | In progress |
| HIPAA-PRIV-ACCESS | HIPAA Privacy Rule | 45 CFR 164.524 | Patient right of access | Let patients see and get a copy of their records. | Visit summary in Phase 2; patient portal in Phase 6. | Not started |
| US-STATE-LAWS | State privacy and medical record laws | Depends on state | State requirements | Some states add rules on minors, sensitive conditions and breach notices. | Counsel lists the states served and their rules. | Not started |

## India

| Code | Law | Citation | Requirement | What the law asks | What HIMS does | Starting status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| DPDP-NOTICE-CONSENT | DPDP Act 2023 and Rules 2025 | Sections 5, 6; Rule 3 | Notice and consent | Tell people what data is processed and why; obtain consent or rely on a lawful use. | Designed for registration in Phase 2 (D9). Counsel confirms the basis for treatment. | Not started |
| DPDP-SECURITY | DPDP Act 2023 and Rules 2025 | Section 8(5); Rule 6 | Reasonable security safeguards | Encryption or masking, access control, logging, monitoring, backups and contracts. | Access control, encrypted secrets and identifiers, audit log. Backups come with hosting. | In progress |
| DPDP-LOGS | DPDP Rules 2025 | Rule 6 | Keep logs for at least one year | Keep logs and related data for breach detection for at least one year. | Audit events are never deleted; system logs are set up at hosting. | In progress |
| DPDP-BREACH | DPDP Act 2023 and Rules 2025 | Section 8(6); Rule 7 | Breach notification | Tell the Board and affected people without delay; detailed report to the Board within 72 hours. | Incident log sets the deadlines and alerts before they pass. | Implemented, not verified |
| DPDP-RETENTION | DPDP Act 2023 and Rules 2025 | Section 8(7); Rule 8 | Erase data when no longer needed | Erase personal data once the purpose is over, unless another law requires keeping it. | Retention schedule drafted in docs/compliance/retention-schedule.md. Daily purge of sign-ins, messages, invitations, resets and security logs once the hospital sets periods, with legal hold (Compliance, Retention tab); periods need counsel. | Not started |
| DPDP-RIGHTS | DPDP Act 2023 and Rules 2025 | Sections 11 to 14 | Rights of the person | Access, correction, erasure, grievance redress and nomination. | Corrections are audited today; a request process comes with Phase 2. | Not started |
| DPDP-CHILDREN | DPDP Act 2023 and Rules 2025 | Section 9; Rule 10 | Children's data | Verifiable parental consent for children; counsel checks health exemptions. | Guardian recorded at registration in Phase 2. | Not started |
| DPDP-PROCESSORS | DPDP Act 2023 | Section 8(2) | Contracts with processors | Use processors only under a valid contract. | Vendor list in docs/compliance/vendors.md. The contracts are the hospital's. | Not started |
| DPDP-CONTACT | DPDP Act 2023 and Rules 2025 | Section 8(9); Rule 9 | Published contact | Publish who answers questions about personal data. | The hospital names the person; shown in the privacy notice in Phase 2. | Not started |
| CERTIN-REPORTING | CERT-In Directions (28 April 2022) | IT Act section 70B(6) | Report cyber incidents within 6 hours | Report listed cyber incidents within 6 hours of noticing them. | Incident log sets a 6-hour deadline and emails the compliance team at once. | Implemented, not verified |
| CERTIN-LOGS | CERT-In Directions (28 April 2022) | IT Act section 70B(6) | Keep system logs 180 days in India | Keep logs of systems for a rolling 180 days within India. | Audit events are kept; system logs are set up at hosting. | In progress |
| CERTIN-TIME-SYNC | CERT-In Directions (28 April 2022) | IT Act section 70B(6) | Synchronise clocks | Synchronise system clocks to a reliable national time source. | Set up at hosting. | Not started |
| IN-IT-ACT-SPDI | IT Act 2000 and SPDI Rules 2011 | Section 43A | Sensitive personal data practices | Reasonable security practices for health data; counsel confirms status as DPDP commences. | Same safeguards as DPDP-SECURITY. | In progress |
| ABDM-HDMP | ABDM Health Data Management Policy | Consult ABDM documents | ABDM participation | Consent-based exchange and security rules for ABHA and health records, if the hospital joins. | ABHA numbers recorded as not verified in Phase 2; ABDM integration in Phase 6. | Not started |
| AADHAAR-STORAGE | Aadhaar Act 2016 and UIDAI rules | Counsel to confirm | Storing Aadhaar numbers | UIDAI rules restrict storing full Aadhaar numbers. Decision D6 allows entry for now. | Encrypted and masked when built in Phase 2. Must be settled before real patients. | Not started |
| IN-MEDICAL-RECORDS | Medical council regulations and state rules | Counsel to confirm | Medical record retention | Keep patient records for the required period; medico-legal cases often longer. | Nothing is deleted; docs/compliance/retention-schedule.md lists what counsel must set. | Not started |

## Both countries

| Code | Law | Citation | Requirement | What the law asks | What HIMS does | Starting status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ALL-THREAT-MODEL | HIMS specification | Spec 23 | Threat model and risk assessment | Completed and reviewed before go-live. | docs/compliance/threat-model.md and the risk register; needs security review. | In progress |
| ALL-RETENTION | HIMS specification | Spec 13.3, 13.4, 23 | Retention and legal hold | Documented retention, deletion and legal-hold rules. | docs/compliance/retention-schedule.md; retention periods, legal holds and a recorded daily purge (Compliance, Retention tab); periods need counsel. | In progress |
| ALL-INCIDENT-DRILL | HIMS specification | Spec 27.5 | Incident response readiness | Run through the incident process before go-live. | Runbook and incident log exist; the drill is the hospital's. | Not started |
| ALL-COUNSEL-REVIEW | HIMS specification | Spec 13, 26.7 | Counsel review | Qualified counsel validates this matrix against the real services. | This register and docs/compliance are prepared for that review. | Not started |
